newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt must submit tax code to get IMF cash.
newsitem.headline: Russia govt must submit tax code to get IMF cash.

text.p: The IMF has agreed with the Russian government that there will be no disbursements under its three-year $10 billion loan until after the government submits its full tax code to parliament, IMF managing director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday.
"I must tell you that the government has accepted that the transmission of the tax code to the State Duma be a prior action to the disbursement of the IMF," Camdessus said.
Speaking in English at a news conference, Camdessus, who is French, added:
"They accept to give such a priority to the transmitter of the tax code to the State Duma, they accept that we don't start paying them before they have completed this work."
The conservative-dominated Duma (lower house of parliament) has not yet approved the first part of the tax code, which will underpin Russia's revenue and spending plans.
But the government has not yet submitted the complete document. Reform chief Anatoly Chubais said last month that his team was racing to complete work on the document.
Camdessus also told the news conference that he had not had detailed discussions with Russian officials about the release of monthly tranches of the IMF's loan to Russia.
"What we have discussed so far is the 1997 programme for the country," he said.
"We will possibly discuss (the monthly tranches) later on. We found it more important to focus on the big numbers."

A statement signed by Camdessus and by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, released before the news conference, said both sides agreed Russia needed to boost tax revenues, approve a new tax code and deepen structural reforms.
It said the two sides were now ready for their "final technical discussions" on a loan programme for 1997-98 and that Camdessus was ready to present an agreement to the IMF board soon.
